messages.content: You are the librarian of an automated numerical-analysis lab. You only ever cite documents from the list you are given, by their ids in square brackets; you never add documents, dates or results from memory. Answer with JSON only.

Scoreboard time_integrators, section ssp, entry:
{
 "id": "ssp-s4-p2",
 "best_known": 3.0,
 "status": "solved",
 "method": "SSPRK(s,2): s-1 Euler steps of dt/(s-1) and u_s = u0/s + (s-1)/s (u_{s-1} + dt/(s-1) F); coefficient s-1",
 "source": "Kraaijevanger (1991) for the bound s-1 on second-order methods; the family in Gottlieb, Shu & Tadmor, \"Strong stability-preserving high-order time discretization methods\", SIAM Review 43 (2001), and Ketcheson (2008).\n",
 "stages": 4,
 "order": 2
}

Documents from the reading list (summaries written by the lab; cite only these):
1. [gottlieb-shu-tadmor-2001] 2001: Strong stability-preserving high-order time discretization methods. The survey that names strong stability preservation: SSP Runge-Kutta and multistep methods, the optimal s-stage second-order family with coefficient s - 1, and the use of downwind operators for methods that need negative coefficients. Results: the s-stage second-order SSP family has coefficient s - 1
2. [ketcheson-2008] 2008: Highly efficient strong stability-preserving Runge-Kutta methods with low-storage implementations. SSP methods with many stages and low storage: the ten-stage fourth-order method with coefficient 6, and the family with n^2 stages of order 3 and coefficient n^2 - n built from Euler steps of size dt/(n^2 - n) and one convex combination, shown optimal among methods with that many stages. Results: SSPRK(10,4) with coefficient 6; SSPRK(n^2,3) with coefficient n^2 - n
3. [spiteri-ruuth-2002] 2002: A new class of optimal high-order strong-stability-preserving time discretization methods. SSP Runge-Kutta methods with more stages than their order have larger coefficients: the four-stage third-order method has coefficient 2 and the five-stage fourth-order method coefficient 1.508, both found by numerical optimization and both better per stage than the classical SSP methods. Results: SSPRK(4,3) with coefficient 2; SSPRK(5,4) with coefficient 1.508
4. [shu-osher-1988] 1988: Efficient implementation of essentially non-oscillatory shock-capturing schemes. Writes Runge-Kutta methods as convex combinations of forward Euler steps so that any property forward Euler has under a CFL restriction (such as being TVD) carries over with the time step multiplied by the smallest ratio of the combination coefficients. Gives the two-stage second-order and three-stage third-order methods with coefficient one, now called SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3). Results: the Shu-Osher form: convex combinations of Euler steps; the CFL coefficient as the minimum ratio alpha/beta; SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3) with coefficient 1
5. [gottlieb-ketcheson-shu-2011] 2011: Strong Stability Preserving Runge-Kutta and Multistep Time Discretizations. The monograph on SSP methods: the theory through the radius of absolute monotonicity, the canonical Shu-Osher form, tables of optimal explicit and implicit methods and their coefficients. Results: tables of optimal SSP coefficients by stages and order
6. [gottlieb-shu-1998] 1998: Total variation diminishing Runge-Kutta schemes. Proves that among two-stage second-order and three-stage third-order methods the Shu-Osher methods have the largest CFL coefficient (one), and that every four-stage fourth-order method needs a negative coefficient in its Shu-Osher form, so classical RK4 is not SSP without a downwind operator. Results: SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3) are optimal with coefficient 1; no four-stage fourth-order explicit method has nonnegative Shu-Osher coefficients
